rv.q: It’s just a pity that, much of the time, Chaka seems to be a guest at her own party.
If the script is sappy, Burke's voice is mercifully magnificent, although she could do with fewer distracting hand gestures.
I'm Every Woman boasts an exceptionally talented cast whose extraordinary vocal performances consistently honour Chaka Khan 's remarkable catalogue.
As biographies go however, it feels relatively superficial.
Then again, the show’s momentum is slowed to an extent anyway by the decision to make forays into the lives of other singers.
As a portrait of one of contemporary music’s most influential artists, it feels frustratingly incomplete.
Chaka Khan's life and legacy deserve so much more than this.
It’s far deeper, more emotionally affecting and ultimately more joyous than we were expecting so we think this Chaka Khan musical is our surprise hit of the summer.
Alexandra Burke plays Chaka, leading a cast at the top of their game vocally through the 29 songs that thread through the show.
It’s an entertaining tribute that captures the scale of Chaka Khan's legacy, even if it doesn't always capture the depth of the woman herself.
I'm Every Woman needs an awful lot of work.
I’m Every Woman is more of a passive watch than an active one, and that doesn’t really align with the energy and commanding presence of a musical icon as fierce as Chaka Khan.
In its current form, I’m Every Woman is a muddled affair that isn’t befitting of Chaka Khan herself or the jukebox musical genre it longs to be a part of.
Dull and oblivious, I’m Every Woman is more likely to make viewers want to pack their bags and avoid sitting through stuff like that.
Even so, all that talent doesn't add up to a great musical.
The choreography itself (by Ebony Clarke) is playful and vibrant – the perfect accompaniment to The Queen of Funk’s soundtrack.
This show is an uplifting, empowering and deeply moving production that celebrates not only an extraordinary artist but also the enduring strength of women.
It remains an imperfect but heartfelt tribute.
‘I’m Every Woman: The Chaka Khan Musical’ is a vibrant celebration of Black female strength, with a surprisingly open heart.

cn.t: Alexandra Burke's powerhouse vocals electrify this Chaka Khan musical, but critics find the jukebox bio hampered by pedestrian storytelling and uneven dramaturgy that fails to match the icon's legendary catalog.
